We investigate topological T-duality on almost abelian solvmanifolds, a class of spaces that includes well-known examples like Heisenberg and Kähler-Cartan solvmanifolds. By focusing on models with maximal torus actions, we demonstrate that these spaces typically possess free $T^2$-actions, enabling the application of T-duality frameworks established in prior research.

This paper introduces a novel embedding method for minor-free graphs on surfaces that maps an $n$-vertex graph with treewidth $k$ into a line graph with treewidth $O(k)$ and at most $n^{1+o(1)}$ edges. As a direct consequence, we establish that the problem of finding a maximum independent set is W[1]-hard with respect to treewidth when parameterized on surfaces. Furthermore, we demonstrate the hardness of approximating the maximum independent set within a factor of $n^{1-\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon > 0$ in the same class of graphs, assuming the validity of the Strong Unique Games Conjecture.

This work establishes that the asymptotic behavior of a discrete-time dynamical system is entirely determined by its C1-smooth, strongly monotone nature. Specifically, it is proven that any such system converges to a globally asymptotically stable fixed point. This finding serves as the discrete counterpart to a well-established result concerning continuous-time dynamical systems. Additionally, the study presents a novel class of discrete-time systems featuring a unique globally asymptotically stable orbit that is neither fixed nor periodic.

Variational quantum eigensolvers (VQE) are anticipated to be a primary method for simulating quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware. A critical aspect of this approach is selecting a parameterized ansatz that balances circuit depth with expressivity. While ansatzes based on fermionic excitations are widely used, they often require deep circuits due to the complexity of mapping fermionic operators to qubits. This study demonstrates that using excitations defined by qubits allows for ansatzes that are significantly more efficient in terms of circuit depth while maintaining comparable expressivity. We validate this by applying qubit-excitation-based ansatzes to various molecules, showing that they achieve similar results to fermionic excitations with much shallower circuits. Furthermore, we examine the impact of different orbital selection strategies on performance. Our findings indicate that while excitations between the highest and lowest energy orbitals yield the best results, restricting excitations to the virtual and occupied orbitals—mimicking the standard fermionic approach—produces comparable performance with a marked reduction in circuit depth.

Deep generative models are increasingly utilized for unsupervised representation learning, yet they often struggle with optimization difficulties and limited representational capacity. This paper introduces a novel approach that addresses these challenges by employing a Deep Generative Decoder (DGD) capable of learning a low-dimensional, continuous latent space. Unlike variational autoencoders (VAEs), the proposed framework does not require an encoder, thereby eliminating the need to jointly optimize two neural networks. This design choice streamlines optimization, enhances representational capability, and allows for the direct application of various supervised tasks. Empirical evaluations on image datasets demonstrate that the method surpasses state-of-the-art VAEs in both image quality and downstream task performance. Furthermore, the framework is versatile, supporting extensions to semi-supervised learning, out-of-distribution detection, and the integration of multiple data modalities.

The expansion history of the Universe can be probed using the cosmic microwave background (CMB), which is sensitive to gravitational waves. We investigate the impact of a primordial stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) on the CMB, focusing on scenarios where the background is detectable by future space-based interferometers. We demonstrate that such a background can induce a shift in the CMB acoustic peaks that mimics a variation in the sound horizon, thereby potentially causing misinterpretations of the CMB data. We quantify the constraints that the CMB imposes on the SGWB, specifically regarding the background's frequency and amplitude. We also examine the implications for the CMB when the SGWB is detectable by next-generation detectors. We conclude that the CMB can tightly constrain the SGWB, ensuring that these gravitational waves do not significantly affect the CMB. This study reports the detection of 10 volatile species within the inner coma of comet C/2015 ER61 (ATLAS) using the 3.5-meter Isaac Newton Telescope at the Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos on the Canary Islands. The observed molecules include CO, CO$_2$, H$_2$CO, H$_2$CS, H$_2$S, HCN, HNC, CH$_3$OH, CH$_3$CN, and CH$_3$CH$_2$CN. These detections were achieved via near-infrared spectroscopy in the 2.8–3.6 $\mu$m range, employing both the near-infrared Integral Field Unit (NIFS) and long-slit spectroscopy. The study provides the first measurements of H$_2$CO, H$_2$CS, H$_2$S, HCN, HNC, CH$_3$OH, CH$_3$CN, and CH$_3$CH$_2$CN in a long-period comet, while also reporting CO$_2$ and CH$_3$CH$_2$CN abundances for this comet for the first time. Additionally, this work offers the first detection of HNC in a long-period comet. The study further calculates production rates for all detected molecules and compares these values with data from other comets.

This paper introduces an unsupervised speech synthesis framework that converts a speaker's voice into a target voice without requiring paired data. The proposed approach relies on two key components: a speaker-conditioned autoencoder and a speaker embedding network. The autoencoder is trained using a generative adversarial network (GAN) framework to map acoustic features from one speaker's domain to another's. Simultaneously, the embedding network learns robust speaker representations by maximizing mutual information between them and acoustic features while minimizing embedding variance. Experiments conducted on the LJSpeech dataset demonstrate that our unsupervised system achieves performance comparable to supervised baselines, with mean opinion scores (MOS) of 3.50 and 3.49 for our proposed method and a supervised system, respectively.

This paper examines the dynamic evolution of the fractional energy density, defined as the ratio of dark energy density to the sum of dark energy and dark matter densities. We demonstrate that this ratio fails to represent a real universe whenever it drops below -1 or exceeds 1. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that the corresponding equation of state parameter cannot surpass the limits of -1 or 0. Consequently, the ratio of fractional energy density cannot serve as a viable dark energy model.

Multi-Objective Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Programming (MO-MINLP) problems are prevalent in real-world applications, yet they remain difficult to solve due to their NP-hard nature. While Evolutionary Algorithms (EAs) offer a viable solution, they typically require significant computational time. This paper introduces a hybrid method combining Branch-and-Bound (BnB) with the NSGA-II algorithm to address these challenges. The proposed approach operates in two phases: first, the BnB process generates a Pareto-optimal set of integer solutions, and second, these solutions are utilized to initialize the population of the NSGA-II evolutionary algorithm. Experimental results indicate that this strategy significantly reduces the execution time of MO-MINLP problems compared to standard EAs, while simultaneously delivering superior solution quality.

This work introduces several connectedness conditions within the realm of internal Lie groupoids over Diff-manifolds, demonstrating that their essential characteristics mirror those of classical (external) Hausdorff groupoids. Additionally, we examine the topology generated by these connectivity criteria on the space of groupoids and explore how this topology relates to the underlying manifold's topology.

The Dynaswap architecture is designed to enhance the security of cyberinfrastructures by integrating a specialized, isolated network layer that functions as a cyberinfrastructure backbone. This approach enables the delivery of secure data services, such as encrypted data transfer, to cyberphysical systems. Dynaswap achieves this by utilizing a dedicated hardware accelerator to execute cryptographic operations, which are orchestrated by a custom-designed network protocol stack. This architecture is implemented on the Dynaswap hardware platform, featuring a reconfigurable logic core equipped with an integrated, high-performance cryptographic coprocessor. This paper presents the Dynaswap architecture, detailing its hardware platform, cryptographic coprocessor, and protocol stack. Furthermore, it evaluates the architecture's performance and security efficacy through experiments conducted on a cyberphysical testbed.

Aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) is a critical component of opinion mining, focusing on determining the sentiment polarity toward specific aspects within a review. While prior research has primarily targeted explicit sentiment expressed directly by adjectives, this study addresses implicit sentiment, where the sentiment polarity is conveyed through non-sentiment words. To achieve this, we introduce a novel approach that integrates sentiment polarity determination with aspect extraction into a single unified framework. This method utilizes a sentiment polarity classifier trained on sentiment labels derived from sentiment dictionaries to identify implicit sentiment polarity. Experimental results demonstrate that this unified framework outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

This paper introduces a new method for conducting mediation analysis within stratified case-control studies that include binary exposures. It leverages the case-control framework to estimate conditional odds ratios for the exposure-outcome, exposure-mediator, and mediator-outcome relationships. By applying the Stratified G-computation algorithm, the authors derive consistent estimates for these relationships and the subsequent mediation effects. The approach is validated through simulations and illustrated using data from a case-control study examining the role of body mass index in the link between oral contraceptive use and breast cancer risk.

This study addresses the maximization of secrecy rate in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enhanced multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, where the RIS is positioned within the transmitter's (trans) and receiver's (receiver) line of sight. The optimization problem involves beamforming vectors at both ends and the reflection coefficients for the passive RIS, subject to unit-modulus constraints on the latter. To address the non-convex nature of this problem, we propose an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. This method decomposes the original problem into two sub-problems: first, optimizing the RIS reflection coefficients given fixed beamforming vectors using a semidefinite relaxation (SDR) approach; second, updating the beamforming vectors while the RIS parameters remain constant via block coordinate descent. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AO method achieves near-optimal performance with significantly lower computational complexity.

Few-shot Continual Learning (CSL) addresses the challenge of retaining old knowledge while learning new tasks without forgetting previous ones. This study introduces a novel approach named "Exploratory Function," designed to enhance task separation and knowledge retention. By utilizing an exploration metric, the method identifies and isolates task-specific features, effectively preventing knowledge interference across different tasks. Empirical evaluations across various continual learning benchmarks demonstrate that this function significantly improves performance. Additionally, the method is lightweight, requiring minimal computational overhead and memory usage.

The Parker Solar Probe (PSP) is designed to explore the Sun's immediate environment by approaching within 10 solar radii ($R_{\odot}$). This study presents the first comprehensive PSP data regarding solar wind energy flux, covering the period from October 2018 to June 2019. Analysis reveals an average energy flux of $1.1 \pm 0.2$ mW m$^{-2}$ at 1 $R_{\odot}$, which decreases to $0.2 \pm 0.1$ mW m$^{-2}$ at 9.5 $R_{\odot}$, aligning with the inverse-square law. The study further identifies a correlation between energy flux and the radial distance of the Parker Spiral, with higher fluxes observed in regions closer to the spiral's axis. Additionally, the data shows a correlation with the magnetic field's azimuthal component ($B_{\phi}$), where increased $B_{\phi}$ corresponds to elevated energy flux.

We define a "locally trivial" $G$-C*-algebra as the commutant of a specific class of unitary representations of a compact Lie group $G$. This framework enables the construction of noncommutative "G-equivariant" vector bundles equipped with connections. Notably, these bundles are locally trivial $G$-C*-algebras endowed with a connection. These algebras and their connections are characterized by a pair consisting of a standard connection and a corresponding unitary representation of $G$. Furthermore, we establish a specific condition for these bundles to be isomorphic.

We demonstrate that any MAD family can be established by forcing. Additionally, we show that any two models containing MAD families of the same cardinality can be connected via a forcing extension. These findings resolve questions originally posed by Baumgartner and Shelah.

This study investigates the impact of $q$-deformation on phase transitions within an optomechanical setup featuring two cavity modes and two harmonic oscillators, where one oscillator is Raman coupled to each mode. The analysis reveals that $q$-deformation significantly influences the phase transition order in the system. Furthermore, the research examines the impact of two-mode squeezing on $q$-deformed phase transitions, highlighting that while squeezed light substantially alters the transition order, it can also facilitate a second-order transition to become first-order.

We demonstrate that classical bodies within the Two-Rotors Model can exhibit R-negative scissors states, a phenomenon absent in quantum mechanics. These states possess a negative moment of inertia regarding the relative angle between rotors, a characteristic that renders the classical configuration unstable against specific perturbations. In contrast, the corresponding quantum system lacks these negative inertia states, thereby ensuring stability. Consequently, the quantum version of the model can be solved using the standard separation of variables technique.

This study introduces a cell-average based neural network approach for solving the Euler equations, utilizing a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework. The architecture employs a single continuous network across the entire domain, with activation functions and loss functions specifically adapted to handle discontinuities. The cell-average technique ensures network stability by preventing oscillations near shocks and allows for the use of significantly larger time steps compared to traditional numerical methods. Additionally, the method's versatility is demonstrated by its ability to resolve complex shock structures, such as those in a shock-vortex interaction scenario, without relying on refined mesh grids.

The ALICE upgrade at the LHC aims to enhance ALICE's capabilities in measuring heavy-flavor production and low-mass dielectrons, while also extending its reach to higher luminosities. This upgrade involves a new silicon pixel detector with a silicon tungsten composite structure, which ALICE is currently developing. This paper outlines the design, fabrication, and testing of this novel sensor, along with its integration into a readout system featuring a new front-end ASIC.

The connection between quantum field theory and gravity is explored through the lens of the Unruh effect and Hawking radiation. The Unomb effect describes how an accelerating observer perceives a vacuum as a thermal bath, while Hawking radiation refers to the thermal emission from black holes. This work investigates how these phenomena can be modeled using a scalar quantum field theory on flat spacetime, treating black holes as mirrors. By analyzing the relationship between the mirror's trajectory and the resulting radiation, we uncover a parallel between Hawking-like emission and thermal particle production associated with the Unomb effect. This study provides insights into the quantum aspects of black holes and their radiative behavior.

Event Extraction (EE) is a critical information extraction task focused on identifying events within text and delineating their specific attributes. This paper introduces a novel approach to EE that leverages the interdependencies among event elements. The method employs a multi-task learning framework utilizing a pre-trained language model, which simultaneously performs event detection, argument detection, and argument role labeling. The proposed technique is evaluated on the EE2019 dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to the current state-of-the-art methods.

We establish a novel version of the Kato equation concerning differential forms on smooth manifolds. By leveraging this finding, we present a differentially commutative (d.c.) formulation of the JTKT identity within a specific graded category. This framework enables the construction of a homotopy operator for forms on a Poincaré dual space, thereby yielding a concise proof of Stokes' theorem. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Chasles-Sullivan-Sullivan (ChS) cap product admits a representation through a matrix-vector form utilizing a homotopy operator derived from a specific resolution of a Poincaré dual space, thereby offering a new proof of the Chasles-Sullivan (ChS) cap theorem.

This study investigates the X-ray variability of high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) by analyzing the relationship between their X-ray luminosity and the fractional root-mean-square (RMS) variability. We examined 10 HMXBs using XMM-Newton data, covering a luminosity range of $10^{37}$ to $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and compared our results with the variability characteristics of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). Our findings indicate that HMXBs exhibit lower fractional variability power than LMXBs, a trend that persists even after accounting for spectral hardness ratios. We propose that the stellar wind in HMXBs acts as a smoothing mechanism, reducing observed variability. Additionally, we explored the impact of wind density profiles on this effect, determining that a power-law distribution with a density exponent $\alpha \geq 2$ is necessary to replicate the reduced variability seen in HMXBs.

We investigate a quantum field theory featuring a background tensor that breaks Lorentz invariance, specifically focusing on a scenario where this aether is not abelian. This non-abelian aether undergoes its own dynamical evolution, allowing it to transition between different vacuum states. Our analysis examines the quantum field's behavior within this framework, focusing on the zero-point energy and the resulting stress-energy tensor. A key finding is that the stress-energy tensor acquires an additional component driven by the aether's evolution, which breaks the standard trace anomaly. This phenomenon arises because the aether's dynamics modify the standard renormalization group flow of the coupling constant. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the stress-energy tensor can be decomposed into a conformal part and a part that violates conformality. This non-conformal contribution originates from the aether's dynamics and is proportional to the aether's kinetic term. Finally, we discuss the physical implications of these results for early universe cosmology and the formation of compact objects.

Although recent advancements have propelled the development of integrated semantic and syntactic models, the specific contributions of joint modeling versus independent approaches remain unclear. This study addresses this gap by empirically evaluating the impact of combining versus isolating these tasks on both performance and efficiency. We conducted experiments across three datasets, testing four independent models alongside three variations of joint modeling. Our results indicate that joint modeling enhances performance, with the greatest gains observed in semantics. Furthermore, we demonstrate that joint architectures offer superior efficiency by reducing the computational cost of processing.

We introduce a novel correlation linking the spins of merging black holes to the ejected mass, which aligns with the relationship between spin and recoil velocity. This connection stems from the fact that both phenomena are driven by the anisotropy of gravitational waves. We demonstrate that this correlation holds across various spin configurations, including cases with non-aligned spins. Furthermore, we show that the relation remains valid even when the accreted mass is dominated by neutrinos rather than gravitational waves.

We have conducted a systematic investigation of tidal features in early-type galaxies (ETGs) within the Coma Cluster, utilizing deep, wide-field Hubble Space Telescope images from the Coma Cluster Treasury Program. Our analysis reveals that approximately 10% of massive ETGs exhibit prominent tidal structures, defined as having a flux fraction greater than 1%. These features manifest as diffuse halos, tidal tails, or distinct arcs and filaments. The study also identifies numerous fainter galaxies with flux fractions below 1%, suggesting that the majority of ETGs in Coma possess detectable tidal debris. We further examined the morphological characteristics of these features, noting that while most are diffuse halos, a significant subset displays clear tidal tails or arcs. Additionally, we identified several instances of ongoing galaxy interactions, including mergers and collisions, which are likely responsible for generating these structures. Our findings indicate that tidal interactions are a prevalent phenomenon within the Coma Cluster, with implications for understanding galaxy evolution and the role of environmental factors in shaping galaxies.

This study examines the Azimuthally Symmetric Theory of Gravitation (ASTG), developed by the author, which posits that gravitation includes a repulsive component in polar regions. Under ASTG, the gravitational field in a spheroid is calculated, revealing a negative (repulsive) gravity at the poles and diminished attraction along the equator. This theoretical framework is then applied to model the anomalous free-fall accelerations observed at the poles and equator of Earth, the Moon, and the Sun. The results indicate that the magnitude of this repulsive gravity correlates with the object's rotation speed, suggesting a direct link between rotation and the strength of the gravitational anomaly.

The origin of fast radio bursts (FRBs) remains uncertain, with leading theories including magnetar flares, compact binary mergers, and the activity of supermassive black holes. Recent optical detections of FRBs have sparked debate regarding the nature of these events and the characteristics of their sources. This study presents a systematic analysis of optical data from 10 FRB sources, covering a total of 100 hours of observation. We report no confirmed optical counterparts for any of these sources, though we establish upper limits on the optical fluence and energy release. By applying a magnetar flare model to these energy constraints, we derive limits on the magnetar's spin-down luminosity and magnetic field strength. Our findings indicate that the magnetar flares responsible for FRBs possess energies exceeding $10^{45}$ erg, a magnitude that surpasses the capabilities of typical galactic magnetars. Consequently, our results suggest that FRBs likely originate from supermassive black holes or magnetars situated within active galactic nuclei.

Chirped pulse amplification (CPA) and nonlinear optical (NLO) techniques have become indispensable across numerous sectors, including medicine, manufacturing, and scientific research. Despite their widespread utility, the intricate architecture of CPA-NLO systems presents significant hurdles for automation and control. This paper introduces a novel control framework designed to streamline the operation of these systems. The framework utilizes a modular, object-oriented architecture that facilitates the integration of diverse hardware components and control loops. Furthermore, it employs a virtual environment for real-time simulation and monitoring of system dynamics, enabling the implementation of advanced control strategies. The framework's capabilities are demonstrated through a practical example involving a CPA-NLO system configured for high-precision micromachining.

Generative models are increasingly capable of producing high-quality outputs, yet their ability to create content based on specific user needs remains limited. While diffusion models have recently advanced the state-of-the-art in image-to-image tasks, they struggle to incorporate diverse, multi-modal guidance signals. To address this, we introduce MAGIC, a unified framework that leverages the latent space of state-of-the-art diffusion models to enable image-guided generation using various inputs. By employing a lightweight, generalizable encoder, MAGIC successfully integrates multiple guidance modalities, such as image masks, image crops, and image sketches. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art results in zero-shot multi-modal image inpainting, object removal, sketch-based generation, and partial image completion tasks.

This paper introduces a new RingCT format featuring "stealth addresses" built into the verification process, which is fully compatible with the Monero network. We have developed a novel scheme called Delegated RingCT that streamlines the verification process by offloading it to a trusted party, thereby reducing the cryptocurrency's reliance on heavy cryptographic checks. This optimization significantly lowers the cryptocurrency's transaction size and the associated fees. Additionally, we have created a new proof system known as Proof of Constant Scalar, which is based on the proof of knowledge of a constant scalar and is proven to be sound under the generic group model assumption.

Emittance scans are frequently employed to determine the optimal beam optics for experiments and future accelerator designs. This study presents the outcomes of an emittance scan conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) to evaluate the performance of the Low Energy Antiproton Beam (LEAR). The scan characterized the horizontal and vertical transfer functions for both horizontal and vertical planes, covering momentum deviations ($\Delta p/p$) from -1.5% to +1.5%.

Continual learning addresses the challenge of training artificial neural networks on sequential streams of data without access to historical information, thereby preventing the phenomenon known as catastrophic forgetting. While numerous techniques have been developed to mitigate this issue, they often suffer from high computational costs, memory requirements, or limited applicability to specific architectures. This paper introduces a novel approach that leverages the inherent redundancy within artificial neural networks. By employing a binary mask to selectively disable a subset of neurons, the method retains network functionality using only the remaining active units. This strategy enables the reuse of pretrained models for new tasks, effectively curbing catastrophic forgetting. Empirical results across various benchmark datasets demonstrate that this method achieves performance on par with state-of-the-art approaches while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.

Neural networks have achieved remarkable success across numerous machine learning domains, yet their substantial computational and memory demands hinder deployment on resource-constrained devices. Quantized neural networks (QNNs) address this by scaling down floating-point weights and activations to lower bit-widths, thereby reducing memory usage and accelerating inference. This paper introduces a novel end-to-end training framework for QNNs that integrates a new quantization-aware loss function with a dynamic bit-allocation strategy. Our approach automatically optimizes both the bit precision for each layer and the associated codebooks during the training process. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to existing end-to-end QNN training methods, our framework achieves superior accuracy on the MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet datasets.

Continuum soft robots offer great potential for complex tasks within confined spaces, yet they face intrinsic hurdles such as nonlinear, highly coupled dynamics and significant modeling uncertainties. To address these issues, this paper introduces a data-driven control framework that integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with a model predictive control (MPC) strategy. This hybrid approach utilizes an RL-trained neural network to approximate the robot's dynamics, thereby reducing computational costs and enhancing robustness against model inaccuracies. The method is validated through experiments on a six-degree-of-freedom continuum robot designed for minimally invasive surgery. The results demonstrate that the proposed controller successfully overcomes dynamic nonlinearities and uncertainties, achieving superior performance compared to traditional controllers.

The real Jacobi group $G^J_1(\mathbb{R})$ is defined as the semi-direct product of the special linear group $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ and the three-dimensional Heisenberg group. This study examines the holomorphic discrete series representations of $G^J_1(\mathbb{R})$ by applying a reduction method that maps them to a tensor product consisting of a holomorphic discrete series for $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ and an irreducible unitary representation of the Heisenberg group.

Natural Language Inference (NLI) has recently been applied to fact verification, yet most current approaches focus on unstructured text and overlook rich, domain-specific structured data. This paper addresses the challenge of fact verification using structured data, where the primary difficulty lies in effectively integrating both structured and unstructured information. To address this, we introduce a novel hybrid architecture that merges graph convolutional networks (GCNs) with BERT. This model represents entities and relations within a knowledge graph, utilizing the BERT network to process natural language inputs and the GCN to model the graph's topology. Experimental results indicate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the FEVER dataset.

While recent unsupervised approaches have made strides in generating realistic synthetic images, they often fail to produce data that is sufficiently varied and tailored to specific needs. In contrast, supervised methods can create highly customized images by leveraging labeled datasets, yet their reliance on existing annotations restricts their ability to generate novel classes. This paper introduces a new unsupervised framework designed to produce annotated synthetic data for arbitrary target classes. Our method generates images using a generator paired with a feature extractor, where the architecture is trained via a novel loss function that encourages image features to align with target class embeddings. By extracting features from the model, we achieve high-quality synthetic data that is naturally labeled. Experiments demonstrate that our approach successfully generates realistic images for unseen target classes and produces labeled datasets that rival those created by supervised methods.

We introduce a novel, parallelizable variant of the differential evolution (DE) algorithm designed to address high-dimensional challenges in inference. This method, named LODE (Local DE), integrates DE with local optimization techniques. LDE operates by first executing DE steps to explore the solution space, followed by local refinement of the resulting candidates. The process then repeats this cycle, alternating between global and local search phases. The primary advantage of LDE lies in its ability to effectively navigate difficult, high-dimensional landscapes while maintaining computational efficiency. The method's performance was validated across three specific use cases: inferring parameters for a linear model with Gaussian noise, calibrating a complex nonlinear model, and determining the positions of astronomical objects.

We introduce novel fault-tolerant distance labeling schemes for both undirected and directed graphs. Our approach assigns concise labels to each vertex, enabling the computation of shortest path distances even when a limited number of graph edges are removed. Specifically, we achieve $O(\log n)$ space complexity per label for undirected graphs with $k$ failures, utilizing a construction time of $O(m \log^{k+1} n)$. For directed graphs, we present a scheme with $O(k \log n)$ space per label and an efficient data structure that supports dynamic updates in $O(k \log n)$ time.

We investigate the time evolution of two-particle correlations in a two-qubit system coupled to a dissipative harmonic oscillator, a setup that generalizes the Jaynes-Cummings model. By employing the quantum trajectory method, we demonstrate that the dynamics asymptotically approach a sum of two oscillations, where the imaginary component of the Liouvillian gap determines their respective frequencies. This behavior emerges from a specific trajectory subspace characterized by a vanishing interaction between the system and the environment, allowing the system to exhibit coherent oscillations. We further show that the trajectory-specific Liouvillian governing this subspace is identical to the Liouvillian of the isolated system, confirming that the observed coherent oscillations are intrinsic to the system's natural evolution.

Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples is vital for clinical safety, particularly in high-stakes areas like medical imaging. While deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown promise in this regard, their performance often varies significantly depending on the specific method employed. This study introduces a novel framework designed to enhance the reliability of DNNs for OOD detection in medical imaging. The approach integrates two key components: a specialized DNN architecture and a dedicated OOD detection module. The proposed design leverages the inherent feature distribution of the network, specifically focusing on the manifold structure within the penultimate layer. By applying a manifold-based regularization technique, the framework effectively constrains the DNN's feature manifold, thereby improving the precision of the OOD detector. Experimental results across three medical imaging tasks demonstrate that this method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques, delivering superior performance.

We investigate a two-level system driven by a periodic field and coupled to both a thermal bath and a vacuum electromagnetic field, focusing on the competition between these influences. By analyzing the steady state, we identify a competition between driving, dissipation, and vacuum fluctuations that results in a phase transition, with critical behavior governed by a single control parameter. Furthermore, we examine the system's response to a sudden quench of this parameter, revealing a crossover from a dissipative phase to a non-dissipative one. This transition is characterized by the emergence of long-time memory effects, which are captured by a power-law decay in the autocorrelation function.

This paper examines the convex solution to the Monge-Amp`ere equation defined on the unit ball within $\mathbb{R}^n$, subject to zero boundary conditions. We demonstrate that the convexity of the domain is a sufficient condition for the convex solution to be convex. Furthermore, we establish that the Alexandrov maximum principle holds for convex functions possessing zero boundary data, implying that this data's H\"older continuity is a necessary condition for the solution's H\"older continuity. We also provide a counterexample to illustrate that convex domains are not, in general, a sufficient condition to guarantee the solution's H\"older continuity. Finally, we present an example of a convex function that is not H\"older continuous at the origin.

Time measurement relies on counting periodic events, yet current standards utilize oscillators that are inherently non-periodic. We introduce a theoretical framework for constructing clocks based on stochastic clicking processes, which can be rigorously analyzed using large deviation principles. This approach offers a distinct advantage over traditional methods by eliminating the need for periodicity, thereby removing associated instabilities. We demonstrate the practical viability of this scheme through a standard random telegraph signal and a model of a chemical reaction operating near a bifurcation point. Furthermore, we evaluate the ultimate precision limits for both schemes and compare their performance against conventional periodic oscillators.

The convergence of Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Fog computing aims to deliver a distributed, low-latency architecture capable of handling data-intensive tasks. This paper introduces a novel, distributed, and scalable controller architecture designed to optimize resource allocation for Fog computing applications within an SDN framework. By leveraging a distributed control plane, the proposed approach minimizes latency and network load while ensuring scalability. Additionally, a distributed algorithm is developed to dynamically place virtual machines on Fog nodes, ensuring that specific Quality of Service (QoS) requirements are met.

Pair-wise loss functions facilitate metric learning by optimizing embeddings to minimize intra-class distances while maximizing inter-class distances, thereby facilitating efficient image retrieval. However, a significant limitation is that they require selecting positive and negative training pairs for every data point, a process that becomes computationally prohibitive with large datasets. This paper introduces a novel approach to image retrieval that bypasses the need for explicit pair generation. By employing a specific data augmentation strategy, we convert single-image classification tasks into metric learning problems. This method effectively learns embeddings that align with pairwise objectives without generating pairs, resulting in substantial reductions in both memory usage and computational overhead. Experimental results on the FashionMNIST and CIFAR10 datasets confirm that this augmentation strategy yields performance comparable to state-of-the-art pairwise loss methods.

We introduce a class of holographic tensor networks that exhibit multiple properties essential for quantum error correction, including holographic duality, a semi-classical limit, and inherent tensor network structure. This framework enables the construction of explicit examples meeting these criteria, specifically holographic duals to pure states in low dimensions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in these models, the dual of a small subsystem is an explicit tensor operation acting on that subsystem, thereby establishing a concrete instance of holographic duality realizable through tensor networks.

We present observations of the Galactic Center using the 12-m radio telescope at 1.4 GHz, achieving an angular resolution of 0.5 arcseconds. The data reveal numerous magnetized radio filaments organized into distinct groups, with most exhibiting either straight or bent morphologies. We identified 12 filamentary groups, each containing between 2 and 10 individual filaments. By analyzing the spatial distribution of these filaments within each group, we determined that their positions follow a Gaussian distribution, allowing us to calculate the mean separation distance. Furthermore, we examined the correlation between the lengths of the filaments and their spacing, finding a positive relationship where longer filaments tend to be more widely separated.

This study introduces a new approach to Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) within distribution systems, grounded in a novel power flow formulation. By representing power flows as a polyhedral set, the method accommodates diverse network configurations, including those with distributed generation and multi-phase systems. Consequently, CVR challenges are modeled as linear programming problems, enabling the rapid assessment of reduction strategies. The proposed framework is validated through extensive testing on the IEEE 33-bus system, demonstrating its efficacy.

This study introduces a novel algorithm for nonstochastic bandits and experts problems characterized by delayed settings, where the learner observes the loss of an expert only after a specific delay. While prior research has primarily focused on scenarios where the learner incurs the loss incurred by the experts with a lag, our work examines a more general scenario involving arbitrary delays. We demonstrate that this scenario reveals a fundamental trade-off between the length of the horizon and the magnitude of delay, a relationship that is absent in the specific case of loss delay. Our findings indicate that for any arbitrary delay, the cumulative regret is bounded by $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{KT \Delta})$, where $K$ represents the number of experts, $T$ is the time horizon, and $\Delta$ denotes the maximum delay. This result establishes a significant improvement over the previous best-known bound of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{KT(T+\Delta)})$ achieved by Gupta et al. (2017).

Dialogue-based task-oriented models often rely on reinforcement learning, which can inadvertently degrade lexical diversity. This paper introduces a new framework designed to enhance diversity within this context. We formulate the problem as a Markov decision process (MDP) and define a specialized reward function that encourages varied responses. We also introduce a novel metric to measure lexical diversity specifically tailored to task-oriented dialogues. Experimental results indicate that our approach outperforms strong baselines in boosting diversity without compromising task success rates.

In the 1970s, Kenneth Wilson introduced lattice QCD, a framework enabling numerical investigations of the quantum chromodynamics non-perturbative aspects. This approach discretizes space-time, reformulating QCD as a numerical problem solvable via Monte Carlo simulations. This review examines the non-perturbative dynamics of QCD, focusing on gluons and quarks within the context of the Wilson action. It explores how these dynamics drive phenomena such as confinement and chiral symmetry breaking, and how they influence the low-energy behavior of nuclear matter.

Accurate prediction of loads on offshore wind turbines (OWTs) is essential for optimizing their design and operation. However, existing prediction models often fail to account for the varying uncertainty levels associated with different sea states, a shortcoming that limits their practical utility. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to forecast both load responses and their heteroscedasticity. The model utilizes a Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture to capture temporal dependencies within input data. To address variable uncertainty, the framework incorporates a heteroscedastic autoencoder that models the conditional distribution of load responses. The proposed method is validated using measured data from the 5 MW IEA Offshore Wind Turbine 60-MW Reference Wind Farm. Results indicate that the model achieves high accuracy in predicting load responses, while also successfully identifying the heteroscedasticity of these loads. These findings demonstrate that the framework can effectively predict future load responses while quantifying associated uncertainty levels, thereby offering valuable insights for OWT design and operational strategies.

Social media has become a vital tool for society, enabling users to connect, share information, and communicate. Its utility in disaster management and public relations is evident, particularly during events like the recent earthquake in Turkey and Syria, where platforms like Twitter were extensively used. This paper introduces a novel approach to automatically generating summaries of such posts to create situation reports for disaster management. By utilizing a graph-based attention mechanism, the system identifies key information from Twitter messages related to a specific event and produces summaries that highlight the most critical details. The study evaluates this method using a dataset of 1,500 tweets concerning the earthquake in Turkey and Syria.

A group $G$ possesses property $R$ if every twisted conjugacy class within its first bounded derived subgroup, $G_1$, is infinite. This paper demonstrates that any group exhibiting the Baum-Connes property with trivial assembly map satisfies property $R$. Additionally, we provide specific examples of property $R$-groups that fail to satisfy the Baum-Connes conjecture.

This approach employs a single forward projection to generate an initial estimate, which is then refined through iterative deconvolution. By incorporating continuity constraints, the method effectively suppresses noise, and it is capable of handling data with missing entries. This paper introduces SceNDD, a naturalistic driving dataset focused on scenarios involving overtaking. It captures data from two vehicles traveling in close proximity on a dual-lane highway, utilizing a mobile unit equipped with multiple sensors. The recording includes diverse data streams such as video footage, vehicle telemetry, and driver biometrics (specifically heart rate and electrodermal activity). Furthermore, the dataset features a comprehensive annotation system that labels video frames for scene understanding and traffic signs, while also marking driver states regarding biometrics and scene perception. This paper details the data collection methodology, the driving scenarios, the various sensor technologies employed, and the resulting annotations.

This work examines the area of the entanglement wedge cross section (EWCS) within the context of boundary conformal field theory (BCFT). We demonstrate that the reflected entropy ($S_R$) in a BCFT corresponds precisely to this geometric quantity. Additionally, we derive the universal contributions to the EWCS area when a conformal defect is present, providing explicit formulas for cases involving both codimension-1 and codimension-2 defects.

The COVID-19 pandemic has prompted the deployment of numerous contact tracing applications, raising significant privacy concerns. This paper introduces a privacy analysis of the Open COVID-19 Tracker app, a solution developed by the German government. Our findings indicate that the app's privacy policy is insufficient, as it fails to disclose critical details regarding data collection, usage, and retention practices. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the app's current architecture is vulnerable to various attacks, including those exploiting Bluetooth proximity data, application of a comprehensive attack model that reveals potential risks. These insights underscore the necessity for stricter regulatory oversight and more rigorous privacy safeguards in the design and deployment of digital health technologies.

This study examines how quantum mechanics explains these specific contributions. We demonstrate that these contributions can be precisely accounted for by a classical model in which measurement outcomes are determined by shared, pre-existing values at the source. This model adheres to the principle of local causality, meaning the outcomes depend only on local settings and the shared values, without requiring direct communication between distant detectors. By analyzing the quantum predictions for two-particle states, we show that these correlations arise from the statistical distribution of the underlying local hidden variables. This perspective offers a new way to understand quantum phenomena, suggesting that quantum mechanics can be viewed as a framework describing the evolution of these local values and their measurement. Asteroid clusters are defined as groups of objects sharing similar orbital parameters, often resulting from dynamical interactions such as mean motion resonances or the Kozai mechanism. This study examines the asteroid cluster located within the 3:1 resonance with Jupiter, utilizing data from the NASA Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) and the NEOWISE mission. The analysis reveals that the cluster's radial and vertical dimensions are significantly larger than those of other known groups, a finding attributed to the cluster's origin in a three-body resonance involving Jupiter and Saturn. Furthermore, the study identifies a distinct lack of asteroids with diameters exceeding 100 km, suggesting that the cluster's parent body was relatively small.

This paper introduces ten novel Ramanujan-style formulas evaluating the Hurwitz zeta function at odd positive integers, alongside a demonstration of how these formulas reduce to Ramanujan's original formulas for zeta values.

We employ a neural network to approximate a continuous map that serves as a proxy for a discrete map used in algebraic geometry, enabling the network to learn a map that effectively quotients a space by a group action. We demonstrate this method by approximating the quotient map from the moduli space of vector bundles on a curve to its image within Grassmannian varieties.

Our findings indicate that the angular distribution parameters for $J/\psi+\chi_{c0}$ align well with experimental data, whereas those for $J/\psi+\chi_{c2}$ deviate significantly from measurements. Furthermore, the calculated cross sections for both processes are substantially lower than observed experimental values.

This paper presents a novel approach to efficiently calculating the anisotropic solar irradiance component of the radiative transfer equation. The method employs Gaussian quadrature to numerically evaluate the necessary angular integrals, specifically the anisotropic part of the source term. By selecting optimal nodes and weights for Gaussian integration, this approach achieves high precision with relatively few evaluations. The study derives specific quadrature rules tailored to both spherical and planar geometries, addressing the diverse conditions encountered in radiative transfer calculations. The proposed rules are evaluated through comparison with existing methods, demonstrating that the Gaussian technique offers superior computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. Furthermore, the paper provides implementation details, including algorithms for generating the quadrature nodes and weights, along with example code to facilitate its use.

The Hessian of the loss function, or its generalized Gauss-Newton approximation, serves as a cornerstone for numerous second-order optimization techniques in deep learning. However, the substantial memory requirements and prohibitive computational costs associated with Hessian-based methods have historically limited their application to relatively shallow architectures. This paper introduces a novel approach that leverages the low-rank structure of the Hessian to facilitate its efficient training. Our method employs a factorized representation of the Hessian, utilizing a compact representation for the input-to-hidden weight matrices and an approximation strategy for the remaining dimensions. By applying the Woodbury matrix identity, we can compute the necessary second-order statistics efficiently. Our experiments demonstrate that this technique successfully trains residual networks with depths reaching 120 layers, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the ImageNet benchmark.

This paper investigates the influence of grammatical gender in natural languages on the vector representations of inanimate nouns. We demonstrate that while such gender biases are present, their intensity varies significantly across different languages and semantic categories. Furthermore, we show that these biases can be effectively neutralized using simple techniques. These findings offer valuable insights for developing more equitable word embedding models.

This work examines the relationship between stiffness and the bifurcation of stationary probability measures within a dynamical framework. Specifically, we demonstrate that for a measure-preserving transformation $T$ supporting an ergodic stationary probability measure $\mu$, if $T$ is stiff with respect to $\mu$, then no sequence of non-trivial Dirac measures can converge to $\mu$ under the weak topology. Additionally, we provide an example of a continuous map defined on a compact metric space that admits two distinct ergodic stationary probability measures, where one measure is stiff while the other is not.

Although deep learning has achieved remarkable success in pose estimation, it typically demands extensive annotated datasets for specific categories, which are often difficult and costly to acquire. This paper introduces a new approach to estimate poses for unseen object categories without requiring any pose labels for those new categories. Our method leverages pre-trained object detectors and a pre-trained pose estimation model trained on general objects. By utilizing the detector's class-agnostic bounding boxes and a pre-existing category-agnostic pose model, our approach eliminates the need for category-specific annotations. We evaluate this method on the COCO dataset for zero-shot categories, including "bottle," "bowl," "bus," "chair," "car," "truck," and "train." Our results demonstrate that the method achieves an Average Precision of 60.5% on the COCO test-dev split, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods by 10.5%.

Accurately forecasting traffic conditions is essential for enhancing road safety, mitigating pollution, and optimizing travel time. While numerous machine learning models have been developed for traffic state prediction, they typically rely on limited features such as current traffic states, historical data, and road network topology. This paper introduces a novel deep learning model that leverages additional data features to improve prediction accuracy. Specifically, the proposed method utilizes a multi-input deep learning framework to integrate real-time traffic states, historical traffic states, and traffic flow data. Experimental results demonstrate that this model outperforms existing prediction methods.

This paper introduces a new approach to causal inference that integrates deep learning with causal discovery. We propose a Structural Causal Model (SCM) that unifies the processes of causal discovery and effect identification into a single, unified framework. Within this SCM, we define a new latent space that captures the causal relationships between variables. We then introduce a novel learning algorithm that simultaneously optimizes the latent space representation and estimates causal effects. Our method is evaluated on synthetic datasets with known ground-truth causal structures, as well as on real-world datasets where causal relationships are established through domain expertise. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

The advent of contemporary radio interferometers has enabled the observation of diverse phenomena, including variable sources, pulsars, and transient events. This paper introduces a framework for a radio telescope control system that leverages a domain-specific language (DSL) to define observation strategies. We present a methodology for translating DSL scripts into scheduling plans, which subsequently generate commands for telescope pointing, data acquisition, and storage. Furthermore, we examine the implementation of this system within the MRO, a simulated telescope array, and discuss its potential application to the MWA and future observatories.

Over the past decade, machine learning and artificial intelligence have driven transformative breakthroughs across numerous scientific and technological fields. Their impact on photonics has been particularly profound, with applications ranging from the design of novel materials and nanophotonic structures to the enhancement of optical measurements and imaging systems. This review offers a comprehensive overview of current progress in AI-driven photonics, highlighting both recent achievements and promising future research avenues.

This study introduces a novel approach to movie revenue prediction that leverages both textual and visual data. We propose a deep learning framework utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to automatically extract high-level features from movie descriptions and posters. The framework's effectiveness is demonstrated through extensive experiments on the IMDb dataset, which feature ablation studies, hyperparameter tuning, and comparisons against various state-of-the-art methods. Results indicate that descriptions and posters have a positive impact on revenue, with poster features providing a greater contribution. Additionally, the paper presents a revenue estimation model that incorporates these multimodal features to forecast potential earnings.

The primary objective of power system operation is to maintain voltage levels and frequency within specified operational limits. This paper introduces a control strategy that leverages the inherent frequency-voltage coupling across the grid to regulate both variables. The proposed method utilizes the frequency deviation observed at a specific location to adjust the voltage setpoints of controllable inverters. The authors demonstrate that this control approach can be implemented using standard grid-forming inverters without necessitating any additional communication infrastructure. The effectiveness of this method is validated through simulations on the IEEE 30-bus system, showing that it successfully mitigates the impact of sudden load changes.

The automotive sector is rapidly advancing toward a collaborative ecosystem of systems, where diverse subsystems and external entities exchange data to deliver emergent capabilities such as autonomous driving, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, and remote fleet management. This paper introduces a formal modeling methodology designed to capture the dynamic behavior of such system-of-systems (SoS) architectures. The approach employs a layered framework that integrates discrete event system theory with multi-agent systems to represent both subsystem dynamics and inter-agent interactions. The proposed model is validated using a V2X-based cooperative intelligent transport system (C-ITS) scenario, where vehicles utilize V2X messages to mitigate traffic congestion.

This study investigates the ultraviolet (UV) and soft X-ray spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of blazars, specifically focusing on the effects of Doppler-boosted thermal Comptonization from hot electrons in the accretion disk corona. We analyze data for the broad-lined flat-spectrum quasar 3C 273, which exhibits a prominent UV excess, and the narrow-lined quasar 1H 0707-495, showing a distinct soft X-ray excess. Our findings indicate that both excesses can be effectively explained by invoking a hot disk corona with temperatures in the range of 10^7 to 10^8 Kelvin. This approach aligns with recent theoretical models proposing that the corona's heat originates from viscous dissipation within the accretion disk.

We investigate the stability of stationary points within complex landscapes, modeled as complex functions with numerous real variables. Our focus is on identifying the stability conditions for a specific class of landscapes, defined as complex-valued functions where the imaginary component is the derivative of the real part. In these scenarios, standard saddle points are replaced by Stokes points, which emerge as pairs on the complex plane whenever the imaginary landscape term vanishes. Our analysis demonstrates that stationary points remain stable only if they are separated from Stokes points by a minimum distance. This finding offers a quantitative measure of how close a stationary point can approach the non-analytic regions of such functions. Our results are applicable to various fields, including machine learning, physics, and optimization.

Discriminating pure states is a fundamental task in quantum information processing, where online strategies offer a distinct advantage by enabling the discrimination of evolving pure-state ensembles without halting the system or applying complex post-processing. This study introduces a new class of offline measurement-based protocols that achieve performance comparable to online methods while maintaining system evolution. We demonstrate that these offline protocols can be seamlessly converted into their online equivalents, a capability that facilitates the practical implementation of online strategies in current quantum technologies.

Baryon production is a key component of the QCD framework, yet it remains poorly understood. This study investigates the role of string breakups in this process, utilizing a QCD-inspired string model. We demonstrate that this approach successfully reproduces the baryon-to-meson ratios observed in $pp$ collisions at 7 and 8 TeV, as well as in $p$-Pb collisions at 8 TeV. Furthermore, we apply this framework to $pp$ collisions at 13 TeV, generating predictions for future LHC measurements.

This study examines the impact of solar active region inflows on global travel time variations in helioseismic measurements, which are driven by the sunspot cycle. We utilized a data-driven model to generate synthetic travel time data, incorporating inflow velocities derived from the Helioseismic Magnetic Imager (HMI) and active region locations from the Sunspot Number (SN) dataset. The results indicate that these inflows account for the observed shifts in global travel times throughout the solar cycle. Furthermore, our findings suggest that the impact of inflows on global travel times is more pronounced than previously estimated.

The recent detection of a stochastic gravitational wave background by NANOGrav has reignited interest in early Universe physics. This study investigates the possibility that a network of cosmic strings could be responsible for the NANOGrav signal. We demonstrate that a network with a tension of $\mathcal{G} \sim 10^{-11}$ can produce a background consistent with the NANOGrav data, provided the network evolves within the standard regime of cosmic string dynamics.

Light field technology offers significant advantages for image acquisition, including depth estimation, virtual camera positioning, and the ability to refocus. This paper introduces a novel single-lens approach to capturing full light fields using a diffractive element, specifically a phase plate, which modulates incoming light. We present a mathematical framework for this system and a corresponding reconstruction algorithm based on the Wigner distribution function. The method was validated through simulations and experiments on a digital camera prototype. Results demonstrate that this approach achieves high-resolution light field data with a wide field of view, all without compromising the image quality of the lens.

Current research on vector-based cross-lingual information retrieval primarily relies on two frameworks: contrastive learning and sentence embedding alignment. While contrastive learning has been the dominant approach, recent studies have demonstrated that sentence embedding alignment can also achieve significant performance. This paper introduces a new model that integrates both methods to leverage their respective strengths. We name this approach Cross-lingual Information Retrieval by Embedding Alignment and Embedding by Contrastive Learning (CIA-ELA). The model employs a shared encoder to generate vector representations for both queries and candidate documents in two languages. We then apply contrastive learning to these embeddings and introduce a novel alignment loss function to ensure the resulting vectors from different languages remain geometrically similar. We evaluate CIA-ELA on the cross-lingual document retrieval benchmarks of CLIR-20 and CLIR-21, demonstrating that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

Demographic surveys are fundamental to public health policy, yet their data quality is often compromised by biases stemming from sampling methods. This study introduces a Bayesian hierarchical model designed to estimate individual-level disease prevalence, specifically targeting HIV among women, while correcting for sample-based bias. By leveraging the complex sampling structures inherent in these surveys, the model generates precise population estimates and facilitates robust subgroup analysis. Additionally, it offers flexible tools for visualizing spatial patterns and temporal trends, which are critical for guiding policy decisions. The methodology is demonstrated using data from the Demographic and Health Surveys, with a specific focus on estimating HIV prevalence across various regions and time periods.

We introduce a novel framework for quantum betting that draws inspiration from classical finance, where the concept of "capital" is defined as the inverse of variance. Within this structure, "ergotropy" serves as the measure of capital investment, while "generalized free energy" represents the resulting returns. The study further explores the relationship between ergotropy and different forms of quantum resource theories, specifically examining how resource monotones can be utilized to bound ergotropy.

We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of the electronic and optical characteristics of the two-dimensional Janus monolayer $\alpha$-$\text{InSe}$, focusing on its interaction with various two-dimensional van der Waals semiconductors and insulators. This study reports the first observation of the decay $\Sigma^+ \to p\pi^0$, achieved through a data sample of $1.0\ \mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb detector at the LHC. The analysis identifies an event excess with a statistical significance of $5.1\ \sigma$. This observation establishes the decay as confirmed and yields a branching fraction of $(1.02 \pm 0.34 \pm 0.12) \times 10^{-1}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second arises from systematic sources.

We investigate the evolution of a self-gravitating protoplanetary disk, specifically examining how the radial distribution of mass flux influences the radial drift of solid particles. Our results indicate that when mass flux is concentrated near the inner regions, the disk's inner zone becomes depleted of matter, whereas a mass flux profile that is more extended outward results in a concentration of material in the inner disk. These findings demonstrate that the radial distribution of mass flux is a critical factor in determining the radial drift of solids.

We introduce a novel method for modeling the atmospheric dispersion vector, which is driven by the atmospheric pressure gradient, utilizing data from a single wavelength. This approach leverages the high correlation between dispersion and chromatic effects to enhance modeling accuracy. The model's performance was validated through simulations and compared against existing atmospheric dispersion models. Results indicate that the proposed technique effectively captures atmospheric dispersion, achieving a reduction in root mean square error of approximately 40% to 50% when contrasted with current models. Consequently, this improvement significantly benefits the data obtained from wide-field instruments equipped with Atmospheric Dispersion Correctors (ADCs).

We introduce a hierarchical latent variable model designed for multi-period time series, which integrates a dynamic factor model with a hidden Markov model. This approach models the dynamic behavior of factors through a factor network and identifies distinct regimes via a state Markov chain. We address the challenges of determining factor dimensions and transition probabilities alongside parameter estimation by utilizing a Markov chain Monte Carlo method grounded in Gibbs sampling. The utility of this proposed framework is demonstrated through an analysis of monthly U.S. inflation data.

We present a novel approach to Pontryagin duality utilizing the Bohr compactification of a given topological group. This method relies on the observation that continuous homomorphisms from the source group into any abelian topological group factor through the Bohr compactification. Consequently, the dual group—defined as the collection of these continuous homomorphisms equipped with pointwise operations—is established as the group of continuous functions mapping the Bohr compactification to the circle group.

The rapid evolution of deep learning has generated significant excitement within the technology sector, yet it also raises critical ethical questions. This paper examines the ethical challenges inherent in deep learning, including privacy, bias, and accountability, and proposes a framework for addressing these concerns. The proposed approach emphasizes the need for transparency, explainability, and fairness in deep learning systems, and outlines strategies for implementing this framework in practice.

We investigate a supersymmetric framework featuring a right-handed neutrino that functions as dark matter. This model incorporates a $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge symmetry, which is spontaneously broken at a high energy scale, leaving a light $Z'$ boson. We demonstrate that $s$-channel resonant production of neutrino dark matter via this $Z'$ boson can account for the observed relic density. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting parameter space is consistent with all existing experimental constraints, including those from LHCb, and remain viable under current direct detection limits.

This study investigates a wireless powered communication network (WPCN) where a multi-antenna base station (BS) simultaneously transmits energy and data to a single-user mobile device (MD) capable of energy harvesting. Additionally, an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) equipped with a massive number of passive units is introduced to enhance system performance. The primary objective is to maximize throughput by jointly optimizing the BS's transmit power and the IRS's reflection coefficients. To address the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we propose an efficient solution utilizing the successive convex approximation (SCA) method. Specifically, we employ the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) technique to handle the non-convexity within the throughput maximization formulation and apply first-order successive convex approximation to manage the non-convex constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves significant performance gains compared to baseline methods.

The study of the $^{136}$Xe decay half-life, alongside the associated axial-vector coupling constant $g_A$, is a critical component of neutrinoless double-beta ($0\nu\beta\beta$) investigations. This research focuses on the experimental determination of the $^{136}$Xe Gamow-Teller strength distribution, a key input for $0\nu\beta\beta$ matrix element calculations. The study employs the $^{136}$Xe($\gamma,\pi^+$) reaction at the HI$\gamma$S facility, utilizing a 31 MeV photon beam and a magnetic spectrometer to measure the outgoing proton spectrum. The resulting spectrum is analyzed using the distorted-wave impulse approximation (DWIA) to extract the giant Gamow-Teller resonance strength. The findings indicate a magnetic dipole giant resonance strength of $1.0 \pm 0.2$ MeV, which aligns with prior theoretical predictions.

We investigate a framework where the origin of dark matter and the baryon asymmetry of the universe are linked through the interplay of a complex scalar field, a fermion, and right-handed neutrinos. In this scenario, the scalar field serves as dark matter, while the fermion is responsible for the baryon asymmetry. Unlike previous models, baryogenesis does not rely on the presence of right-handed neutrinos; instead, they facilitate the generation of the dark matter asymmetry. We demonstrate that the interaction between the scalar field and the neutrinos induces a charge asymmetry in the dark matter sector, whereas the coupling between the scalar field and the fermion generates the baryon asymmetry. Our analysis reveals that the magnitude of the baryon asymmetry is contingent upon the dark matter asymmetry. Consequently, the viability of this model is constrained by the requirement that the produced baryon asymmetry must meet the observational lower bound.

This paper addresses the challenge of controlling unknown dynamical systems, where the primary obstacle is the lack of a system model. While prior approaches utilizing data-driven techniques have achieved significant results, they typically depend on specific assumptions about system properties or data characteristics. This work introduces a new method that leverages side information to enhance control performance. Specifically, we present a data-based control framework that integrates side information to ensure closed-loop stability and achieve optimal performance without requiring a system model. The proposed framework employs a data-driven approach to identify a stabilizing controller by solving a linear matrix inequality (LMI) problem derived from data-driven Lyapunov theory. The side information is then used to refine this solution, improving closed-loop performance. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through simulations on a nonlinear pendulum system, where side information significantly accelerates convergence to optimal performance compared to methods that do not utilize it.

Toda conformal field theories (TCFTs) are defined by affine symmetries of the Weyl group, and their properties are deeply connected to various Lie-theoretic cohomology groups. This article introduces a novel class of twisted equivariant K-theory groups, which are integral to understanding TCFTs. We demonstrate that these twisted groups correspond to the equivariant K-theory of a specific flag manifold associated with the Langlands dual Lie group. This identification allows us to derive new exact sequence relationships among the TCFT K-theory groups and to explicitly calculate them for $A$-type Toda models.

Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are a prominent deep learning approach for generating high-quality synthetic data, yet they remain notoriously difficult to train, particularly at high resolutions. This paper introduces a novel training strategy for GANs that leverages a pre-trained image model to enhance generator quality. The proposed method involves fine-tuning the GAN's generator using a pre-trained model's encoder and discriminator using its decoder. The study evaluates this approach on the CelebA and LSUN-Church datasets, demonstrating that it yields superior results compared to standard training methods. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/ashishjain2000/Pretrained-Model-Fine-Tuning-for-GANs.
